finding: "tp config --extract ... is resolution-preserving by construction: it hoists only a value every task file already carries, so what resolves is unchanged and the change rule never fires" is false, and the counterexample was BUILT AND RUN, not reasoned. --extract preserves resolution only for the task files it scanned; it silently changes it for every resolution context that has no task-level override. Measured in /tmp/tp-r12/extract with the dev binary on the shipped twin field review_converge_on (already in hoistedFields, so it is the exact mechanism row 4 adds audit_converge_on to): one task file spec/a.tasks.json carrying {"review_converge_on":"all"}, empty .tp/config.json, and a second spec spec/b.md with no task file. Before: `tp config --file spec/b.tasks.json --resolved` reports {source: default, value: blocking}. Then `TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp config --extract --force` exits 0 with {"hoisted":["review_converge_on"]}, writes the value into .tp/config.json and strips it from a.tasks.json. After: base b reports {source: project, value: all} — the resolved value CHANGED, unattended, exit 0, no refusal. Mapped onto this release: one task file legitimately carrying audit_converge_on: blocking (an attended, operator-approved opt-in the release is for) makes --extract write blocking into the project layer, and every base with no task-level override then resolves blocking. That is precisely the uncovering §3 says only tp import can do, performed by the one writer §3 exempts from the fence. It is reachable in this repository today: 21 of 46 spec/*.md have no .tasks.json (13 of them planned releases), and `tp audit spec/b.md --status` runs and resolves its workflow with no task file at all — verified, exit 0. It is also reachable with zero missing task files, because it is prospective: after the hoist, the NEXT tp init / tp import creates a task file whose workflow block is empty, and that base resolves blocking from the project layer without any fenced write ever happening. Note also that `tp config --extract --force` is not `tp import --force`: it is in no unattended decision set and was confirmed to exit 0 under TP_UNATTENDED=1.
suggestion: Delete the "by construction" exemption. Either (a) name --extract as a fourth FENCED write path — it is a two-layer write and the change rule is computable there, comparing resolved-before/resolved-after over every discovered base plus the bare project layer; or (b) exclude audit_converge_on from hoistedFields the way commit_strategy is already excluded (config_extract.go carries the precedent and the reason), and reverse §7 row 4 accordingly. Whichever is chosen, §7 needs a row whose mutant is the one just run: hoist from a tree where one base carries the value and another has no task file, and assert the second base's resolved value is unchanged. Row 4 as written asserts only that the field IS hoisted, which is the step that opens the hole.

finding: Row 11's mutant was rewritten this round and the replacement provably does not discriminate; the ground it cites is also false. The new column 4 reads "count the streak as a total rather than a trailing run — v0.35.0 has three clean-under-`blocking` rounds before round 3, so a total reaches 2 one round early". Both halves were measured against the recorded corpus, not reasoned. (a) v0.35.0 has ONE clean-under-`blocking` round before round 3, not three: round 1 carries {warning 5, info 5, error 2} and is unclean under blocking, round 2 carries {info 7, warning 5} and is clean. (b) Trailing-run and total-count convergence were computed side by side over the real per-round severity sequences of both cycles at both audit_clean_rounds values — all eight cells row 11 asserts are IDENTICAL under the two rules: v0.35.0 all 9/9, all@1 8/8, blocking 3/3, blocking@1 2/2; v0.36.0 all never/never, blocking 3/3, blocking@1 2/2. Applying the named mutant leaves every assertion in row 11 green, so the row cannot fail it. The reason is structural: the two rules can only differ after a break in the sequence, and in both cycles the first two clean rounds under each policy are adjacent. Round 11's version of this row named a different mutant ("replay with the field set at round k, which §2.1 says converges no earlier than k + audit_clean_rounds") which does discriminate, since §2.1's own second paragraph states the shift; the rewrite replaced a working mutant with one that cannot fail.
suggestion: Restore a mutant the fixture can kill. The set-at-round-k mutant is one (it moves v0.35.0/blocking from 3 to k+2). Another that discriminates on this corpus: grade blocking on `severity == "error"` alone instead of §2's fail-closed rule — v0.29.0-v0.32.0's 67 out-of-enum rows flip clean under it, though not v0.35.0/v0.36.0's, so the fixture would need to carry one. Whichever is chosen, delete the "three clean-under-blocking rounds" sentence: it is a counted claim the corpus falsifies, and §7's preamble asks each row to state the counting rule it depends on, not to assert an uncounted number.

finding: Six of §7's rows (12, 13, 13b, 13c, 13d, 18) are the first in this spec whose truth depends on the AMBIENT TP_UNATTENDED of the process running the suite, and none states that dependency — which §7's own new preamble demands ("states any file, function or counting rule it depends on"). Measured, not reasoned: internal/cli's test helper builds every child as `cmd.Env = append(append(os.Environ(), "NO_COLOR=1", "TP_HC=0"), extra...)` (runTPEnv, internal/cli/run_driver_test.go), so it INHERITS the parent's TP_UNATTENDED. Running `TP_UNATTENDED=1 go test ./internal/cli -count=1` today produces 20+ failures that do not occur attended, including TestImport_WorkflowPreserved (all three subtests — the exact preservation mechanism §3's remedy 1 depends on), every TestSkipGate_*, TestImport_ConvergenceEnforced/force_bypasses_both_checks, and all four TestUnattendedFence_* guards. So "with TP_UNATTENDED unset" (row 13c) is not achieved by a test that merely does not set it. This is not hypothetical for this release: REFERENCE.md and CLAUDE.md both state tp run gives every child TP_UNATTENDED=1, and the project quality gate a run's implement unit executes is `go test -count=1 -race ./...` — so under tp run, the release's primary self-development model, these rows would run in the wrong mode. Row 18 is the sharpest case because it converts a currently env-INSENSITIVE guard into an env-sensitive one: TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate was run both ways just now and passes both (it asserts a NON-zero exit and "unknown workflow field"), but its reversal to "audit_converge_on IS a known workflow field" asserts that `tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=blocking` succeeds over a fixture with no task-level override — a write that changes the resolved value to blocking and therefore exits 2 under the very fence row 12 adds.
suggestion: State the dependency in the rows and make it mechanical. Every row scoped to the fence should say the environment is set EXPLICITLY per invocation rather than inherited: rows 12/13/13b/13d pass TP_UNATTENDED=1, and row 13c must actively UNSET it (an explicit removal from the child env, not an omission) or the inherited value silently inverts it. Row 18's reversed assertions need the same treatment, and the row should say so, because it is the row that turns an env-neutral guard into an env-dependent one. If the wider inheritance is out of scope for this release, say that too — but the six rows this release writes cannot be left to inherit.

finding: Rows 13b and 13d describe an import over a tree whose task file already carries a task-level `all` — so the target task file EXISTS — but neither states whether it holds tasks, and tp's behaviour splits on exactly that. Measured with the dev binary in /tmp/tp-r12/import: `tp import` over an existing task file that holds real tasks exits 3 with {"error":"task file already exists: spec/a.tasks.json (use --force to overwrite)","code":3} BEFORE reaching anything the fence could evaluate, and `--force` under TP_UNATTENDED=1 exits 2 with the import-force refusal. So on a tasks-bearing fixture: row 13b's assertion "is refused" is satisfied by exit 3 from the pre-existing exists-guard — the test passes green while the audit_converge_on fence is not implemented at all — and row 13d's "two documents import cleanly" cannot pass at all, because both are refused for the same unrelated reason. Only a zero-task init shell (or an absent target) reaches the change rule, which is the precondition neither row states. Row 12 pins "exits 2", so it is safe; 13b says only "is refused", which is the weaker phrasing and the one that fails open. The remaining four document shapes were all run over a zero-task shell to confirm the preconditions do work there: a `workflow` key without the field moved the resolved value from override:all to project:blocking (the refusal case, exit 0 today); omitting the key preserved override:all; carrying "audit_converge_on":"all" preserved it; and `"workflow": {}` behaved identically to the refusal case.
suggestion: State the precondition in both rows: the target is a zero-task init shell, so the import reaches the change rule rather than the exists-guard. Change row 13b's "is refused" to "exits 2 and the message is the audit_converge_on refusal", so exit 3 from the exists-guard cannot satisfy it — this is the same distinction row 14 already draws between this refusal and the command-field one. Row 13d should say the same of its clean imports (exit 0, and the task file's stored workflow still resolves `all`), since an exit-0 import that silently dropped the block would otherwise pass.

finding: §3 illustrates the uncovering import with a document carrying `"workflow": {"review_max_rounds": 5}` — a NON-EMPTY block missing the field. The shape tp itself writes is `"workflow": {}`, and it is refused identically. Verified: model.TaskFile declares `Workflow WorkflowOverride \`json:"workflow"\`` with no omitempty and a non-pointer struct, so EVERY task file tp writes carries a top-level workflow key; `tp init spec/a.md` produces `"workflow": {}`, and importedHasWorkflowKey (internal/cli/import_workflow.go) is a raw top-level key check that returns true for it, so preservation does not fire and the block is replaced by the empty one. Run over the §3 tree, an import of `{"workflow": {}, ...}` moved the resolved value from override:all to project:blocking exactly as the §3 example did. This matters for the remedy §3 now rests on: remedy 1 is "omit the top-level workflow key", which is a shape tp NEVER writes, so a decompose unit that derives its document by round-tripping the init shell (the cheapest way to produce one) lands on `{}` and is refused. The remedy is still available — the unit deletes the key or writes the literal — but §3 reads as though the refused population were documents that name some other field, and a unit reading it may not recognise its own `{}` there.
suggestion: Name `"workflow": {}` in §3 as a refused shape alongside the `{"review_max_rounds": 5}` example, and say why: tp's own writer always emits the key, so an empty block is a REPLACEMENT of the task-level block, not an omission of it. That is one clause, and it is the clause that tells a unit round-tripping an init shell which of the two remedies applies to it.

finding: §6's preamble warns that "A sentence already covered by an item can carry a *second* false clause the item does not name" — and then items 2 and 4, the two largest, are each a one-clause repair of a sentence carrying four or five, with §7 rows 19 and 20 pinning only that one clause. Read against the tree. skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:754-756 is one sentence: "The audit gate is untouched: `engine.Converged`, `engine.ConsecutiveClean`, the stored per-round `clean` flag, the exit code of `tp audit --status --check`, and `next_action`'s three-state audit precedence all behave exactly as in v0.32.0." §2 lines 105-110 names ALL FIVE of those as changing under `blocking`. Item 4 names only the stored `clean` flag, and row 20's assertion is "that paragraph no longer lists the stored per-round `clean` flag among what behaves exactly as in v0.32.0" with mutant "re-add the flag to the list" — a repair that deletes `clean` and leaves the other four passes row 20 green and ships four false clauses. skills/tp/SKILL.md:149 has the identical shape: "**`divergence` gates nothing — it is reporting only.** Convergence arithmetic, the stored per-round `clean` flag, `next_action` and the `--status --check` exit code are unchanged: ... audit convergence still counts every non-PASS row." Item 2 and row 19 repair only the trailing clause (`divergenceCountingSubstring` at internal/cli/docs_contract_test.go:96 is exactly that substring), so the four preceding claims ship false. Separately, §6's replacement sweep criteria do not close the gap either: criterion (b) names "the stored `clean` flag, `next_action` or the `--check` exit code" and criterion (a) "what audit convergence counts", but NEITHER names `engine.Converged`, `engine.ConsecutiveClean` or "Convergence arithmetic" — the two symbols §2 lists first among what changes and the phrase SKILL.md actually uses.
suggestion: Two edits. (1) Widen criterion (b) to the wording §2 already uses: "promises that `engine.Converged`, `engine.ConsecutiveClean`, the stored `clean` flag, `next_action` or the `--check` exit code is unchanged" — so the derivation covers every symbol the release's own downstream list names. (2) Make rows 19 and 20 assert the WHOLE sentence rather than one clause: the mutant should be "repair only the named clause and leave the rest of the sentence standing", which is the repair a reader of items 2 and 4 will actually make.

finding: §6.5 says "The object's third message form counts rows carrying no `role` as `unattributed_open` and warns that the spec-coverage streak may be understated. Nothing else carries that caveat". Two of the three forms carry it, not one: divergenceMessage (internal/engine/divergence.go:180-196) emits the caveat both when every open row is roleless ("none attributed to a role (possibly spec-coverage's)") and when only some are ("including %d with no role, which may be spec-coverage's"); only the unattributedOpen==0 form omits it. The rest of §6.5's measurement checks out exactly and was re-derived: 90 recorded audit round files, 20 roleless non-PASS rows, all `warning` or `info` (9 info, 11 warning), and all 20 sit in four rounds (0.23.0 r1, 0.24.0 r1-r3) every one of which is clean under `blocking` — so "every one of them makes its round clean" holds. Only the carrier count is wrong, and it matters slightly because §7 row 22's fixture ("open rows carrying no `role`") exercises the all-roleless form and would not notice a regression in the mixed one.
suggestion: Say "the two message forms that count a roleless row" rather than "the third message form", or drop the form-numbering and say "whichever message form counts a roleless row". If row 22 is meant to pin both, it needs a second fixture with a mix of attributed and roleless open rows; if it is deliberately pinning only the all-roleless form, say so.

finding: This round deleted §3's three-row rule table (the round-11 snapshot carried it at what is now line 165) and replaced it with prose, but two references to that table survive and now resolve to the wrong thing or to nothing. Line 186: "The change rule catches it because it compares resolved-before against resolved-after; a fence built from the three shapes in the table above would not." §3 (lines 153-217) contains no table at all — the four tables in the file are at lines 44 (§2's value table), 89 (§2's new next_action table), 122 (§2.1) and 334 (§7), so "the table above" now resolves to §2.1's convergence table or §2's next_action table, neither of which holds a fence shape. And §7 row 13b's mutant reads "build the fence from the three shapes in §3's table, which do not reach this input" — it names an artifact the spec no longer has, which is precisely what §7's new preamble forbids ("states any file, function or counting rule it depends on ... A test whose subject the spec cannot name is a decision that has not been made yet"). The three shapes themselves survive in the replacement prose (field-scoped, value-scoped, transition-scoped), so the fix is a wording change, not a restored table.
suggestion: Replace both references with the prose that replaced the table: line 186 becomes "a fence built from the three narrower rules above would not", and row 13b's mutant becomes "build the fence from the three narrower rules §3 rejects (field-scoped, value-scoped, transition-scoped), none of which reaches this input". While there, check row 13's mutant too — it says "a field-scoped or value-scoped fence, both of which refuse the third and deadlock Workflow A step 6", which still reads correctly against the prose.

finding: §6's headline change this round is that the count is replaced by a derivation the task's acceptance runs — but the derivation's scope clause does not reach two of the five items it is meant to subsume. The clause is "across `skills/`, `README.md`, `internal/engine/` and `internal/cli/` doc comments". Item 1's target is a TEST ASSERTION, not a doc comment: `assert.NotEqual(t, 0, code, "audit_converge_on is not a workflow field")` and `assert.Contains(t, stdout+stderr, "unknown workflow field: audit_converge_on")` in internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go — verified present, and the guard holds exactly eleven assert./require. call sites with exactly those two naming the field, as §6.1 says. Item 3's target is a `const`, not a doc comment: `engine.DivergenceHint` at internal/engine/divergence.go:16-19, whose final clause "audit convergence still counts every non-PASS row" was confirmed verbatim and is quoted verbatim by skills/tp/REFERENCE.md and asserted by internal/cli/docs_contract_test.go:145. Under the clause as written a sweeper reads doc comments in those two packages and finds neither. A third near-miss: internal/cli/docs_contract_test.go:96 holds `divergenceCountingSubstring` as a test-local literal — item 2's second half, also a test file. Ran `git grep review_converge_on -- skills/` to check the other half and it does work: it returns SKILL.md:153 (criterion c), SKILL.md:269 and REFERENCE.md:478 (criterion d, both workflow-field enumerations omitting the new field). So the `skills/` half of the scope is sound and the code half is what is narrow.
suggestion: Widen the scope clause to name what the items actually live in: "across `skills/`, `README.md`, and — in `internal/engine/` and `internal/cli/` — doc comments, shipped string constants, and test assertions and test-local literals". Test files matter twice here: item 1 IS one, and items 2 and 3 are each held by a guard whose literal must move with the sentence, which the "three coordinated edits" paragraph already depends on.

finding: Cutting §5 ("What this release deliberately does not contain") and renumbering Non-Goals into its place broke an inbound reference from the spec that took the cut content. spec/0.46.0.md:381-384 reads: "The boundary against `spec/0.45.0.md` §3, which ships first. ... the sentence is here because it was written in `spec/0.37.0.md`'s cut section and recorded in its §5." 0.37.0's §5 is now the Non-Goals list, which records nothing about the spec-hash reset; the record moved to §1's closing paragraph. The paragraph itself survives the compression with its content intact — the five-round history, the vintage-byte/retroactive choice, the `IsLegacyRound` inertness and the pointer to spec/0.46.0.md §8.4 (which exists) are all still there — so this is a pointer to fix, not content to restore. Two other inbound references to 0.37.0 sections were checked and are PRE-EXISTING rather than caused by this round: spec/0.41.0.md:58 and spec/0.34.0-candidates.md:12 both say "`spec/0.37.0.md` §2 carries" the no-`scope`-field deferral, and neither the current §2 nor the round-11 snapshot's §2 mentions `scope` anywhere. Two that resolve correctly: CLAUDE.md:206 ("§5 takes the divergence") is now right because Non-Goals item 1 is the divergence, and spec/0.46.0.md:313/332/334 (§2 and §4) still hit their subjects.
suggestion: Since this spec cannot edit spec/0.46.0.md, record the outbound breakage as part of the cut — a line in §1 saying the spec-hash reset's history now lives here rather than in a numbered section of its own, so the decomposer's sweep task picks up spec/0.46.0.md:384 along with §6's assertions. The pre-existing pair (spec/0.41.0.md:58, spec/0.34.0-candidates.md:12) is worth the same sweep even though it is not this round's doing.

finding: §1's condensed replacement for the cut §5 carries a sentence whose two readings describe opposite mechanisms: "The marker a draft here named, `IsLegacyRound`, is inert — it has marked every audit round since v0.30.0 and changes the streak in 0 of the 15 recorded histories." Measured against the corpus: `engine.IsLegacyRound` (internal/engine/reviewstate.go:503) returns TRUE for a round whose `id_scheme` is absent or empty, and across the 90 recorded audit rounds the field is absent for 21 rounds (v0.23.0 through v0.29.0) and `"slug"` for the 69 rounds from v0.30.0 on. So the predicate marks every round BEFORE v0.30.0 as legacy and NO round since — the inverse of the sentence's literal reading. The intended reading ("the id_scheme marker has been stamped on every audit round since v0.30.0, so a legacy check never fires") is true and does support "inert"; the literal one would make the marker maximally active and contradict the conclusion in the same sentence. The other half checks out exactly: 15 recorded histories carry audit rounds.
suggestion: Say which way it points: "every audit round since v0.30.0 carries the `slug` marker, so `IsLegacyRound` is false for all of them and the check changes the streak in 0 of the 15 recorded histories." One clause, and it stops the reader having to derive the direction from the conclusion.

finding: §2 doubled its next_action decision this round and §7's row did not follow — the exact staleness §7's preamble exists to catch. Round 11 decided one branch ("The recommendation for that branch is decided here"); this round replaced it with a two-row table and the emphasis "**Both affected branches are decided here rather than left to an implementer**", covering (i) clean, not yet converged and (ii) clean, converged. Row 10 is byte-identical to round 11's and pins only branch (ii): "a CONVERGED round holding non-`PASS` rows yields a `next_action` containing the count of accepted rows as a numeral, textually different from an empty round's", with the mutant "branch on `clean` alone, which makes the two strings equal". Nothing pins branch (i), and it is the branch a `blocking` cycle hits repeatedly while the converged one fires once — v0.35.0 under `blocking` would take branch (i) on rounds 2 and every subsequent clean round, and branch (ii) once at round 3. Branch (i) is also the one where the implementation is easiest to get wrong: the default arm of engine.AuditNextAction is reached with `latestRoundHasFindings == false`, so an implementer who threads the count only through the converged case leaves it silently absent from the arm that runs most. The rest of §2's next_action decision checks out against the tree: AuditNextAction's signature is `(specPath string, converged, latestRoundHasFindings bool)`, it has exactly three branches in that precedence, both sinks derive the boolean from `clean` (audit_record.go:125 `!clean` and :390 `!rounds[len-1].Clean`, each carrying the comment §2 says asserts the equivalence), and the count §2 names is available on `--status` without re-reading role files because ReviewRound stores `Findings int`.
suggestion: Split row 10 into 10 and 10b, one per decided branch, each on both sinks — or widen row 10 to "on both audit sinks, BOTH clean branches (converged and not-yet-converged) holding non-PASS rows yield a next_action containing the count as a numeral" with the mutant "thread the count through the converged branch only, leaving the not-yet-converged arm textually identical to an empty round's". §2 names two branches; §7 should name two.
